researchDepth: Structured 12-Driver landscape, existing-source alignment and targeted experimental/contrary checks; not a systematic review of every perception. Reuse Layer and prior-pilot sources without re-auditing external Families.

entityReviews.constructReview: Judged prevalence/frequency of a specified behavior in a named reference group; not actual prevalence or perceived approval.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Estimated peer behavior needs denominator, period and referent. Own behavior and perceived norms can be reciprocally related; intention is not a norm indicator.
entityReviews.timeReview: Momentary feedback and 3/6-month recall are different time scales; neither establishes a universal lag.
entityReviews.unresolved: Weekly drink volume may not match frequency/prevalence without inspecting exact questionnaire; retained feedback effect stays research-needed.

entityReviews.constructReview: Judged approval/disapproval by specified others, not actual expressed approval or perceived behavior prevalence.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Sanction expectations, approval of behavior and approval of the actor are distinct; common referent/items can induce overlap.
entityReviews.timeReview: Current approval judgments do not imply stable cultural norms changed.
entityReviews.unresolved: Behavior outcomes from normative messages do not identify an isolated injunctive perception effect.

entityReviews.constructReview: Expected relational approval after one's specified action; prospectively contingent, unlike others' current approval of behavior.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Expected acceptance and social reward require action/others specified. Need for approval is a motive, not the expectancy.
entityReviews.timeReview: Canonical seconds–minutes onset is not an empirically estimated universal delay.
entityReviews.unresolved: Assigned sources address self-other norm discrepancies or adolescent behavior associations, not exact anticipated-approval manipulation.

entityReviews.constructReview: Judged availability of emotional/informational/instrumental help; not help received or network size.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Support subscales can overlap coping-scale support-seeking items. Objective contacts do not validate perceived availability.
entityReviews.timeReview: Brief offer, months-long package and chronic network resources require separate assessments.
entityReviews.unresolved: Broad interventions do not identify one exact support operation; reuse F02 REL-PSY-016 review and shared CF-0010.

entityReviews.constructReview: Felt acceptance/inclusion/connection with a relevant group; distinguish need for belonging, loneliness and perceived exclusion.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Need-threat belonging items such as outsider wording overlap exclusion checks. Do not infer independent causal mediation from their inverse scores.
entityReviews.timeReview: Transient game ratings cannot establish chronic inclusion or changes to relational ties.
entityReviews.unresolved: No automatic conversion of exclusion effect into a separate independent belonging contribution.

entityReviews.constructReview: Willingness to accept vulnerability toward a specified person, not generalized trust, institutional trust or factual accuracy.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Trust-game transfer bundles risk preference, altruism and strategic expectation. Neurochemical proxies do not define trust.
entityReviews.timeReview: Relationship history differs from immediate transfer choice; enduring change not inferred from a task.
entityReviews.unresolved: Oxytocin and thermal-cue research cannot support a universal exact-person trust effect; source-trust lesson retained.

entityReviews.constructReview: Judgment of fairness of a named procedure, allocation or treatment; explicitly multidimensional.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Procedural/distributive/interpersonal/informational facets are correlated but not interchangeable; acceptance and retaliation are outcomes.
entityReviews.timeReview: Post-encounter judgment differs from long institutional history; no generic hours–years effect estimated.
entityReviews.unresolved: Feature-specific effects cannot become whole-profile improvement; architecture escalation linked to existing feature-scope issue, not repaired.

entityReviews.constructReview: Rightfulness and entitlement to voluntary deference for a specified authority/rule.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Obligation-to-obey, trust, satisfaction and behavioral compliance differ; conflating them can manufacture fairness→legitimacy evidence.
entityReviews.timeReview: Compliance intention measured with legitimacy simultaneously does not establish direction.
entityReviews.unresolved: Policing review's specific legitimacy outcome was not statistically conclusive; no rebranding of trust benefit as legitimacy.

entityReviews.constructReview: Perception of being ignored/rejected/excluded by relevant others; not actual ostracism exposure.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Ignored/excluded ratings directly align in bounded Cyberball tasks; percentage of tosses is a different manipulation check.
entityReviews.timeReview: Immediate retrospective game rating supports transient state only, not chronic exclusion or future withdrawal.
entityReviews.unresolved: Existing REL-SOC-062 is the exposure route; avoid duplicating it or treating this perception as experimentally isolated mediator.

entityReviews.constructReview: Perceived rank/prestige/respect/influence in specified group; not objective income or cross-group status gap.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Subjective SES ladder only partly aligns; health self-report associations are stronger than biological outcomes and mostly cross-sectional.
entityReviews.timeReview: Stable rank histories and immediate rank feedback are not the same manipulation/time scale.
entityReviews.unresolved: No exact effect or causal health edge retained from a subjective-SES association.

entityReviews.constructReview: Perceived unjust disadvantage of one's group relative to salient comparison; not an objective inequality statistic.
entityReviews.measurementReview: Canonical definition lacks an explicit angry-resentment item although key review's RD operationalizations often include affect. Group and individual RD must not be pooled.
entityReviews.timeReview: Comparison, injustice and affect are often measured together; narrative mediator language is not pathway identification.
entityReviews.unresolved: Do not repair definition or manufacture a causal anger edge partly entailed by an affect-containing measure.

entityReviews.constructReview: Current expectations of specified institution's competence/reliability/fairness/openness/integrity; neither person trust nor rightful authority.
entityReviews.measurementReview: OECD perception composites and coarse WGI aggregates do not independently identify real institutional changes. Survey shared method and reciprocal judgment matter.
entityReviews.timeReview: Cross-sectional trust regressions do not establish time ordering; corruption-information experiments differ from actual corruption trajectories.
entityReviews.unresolved: Information can reduce selected trust ratings without changing corruption or legitimacy; exact profile alignment remains unresolved.

existingReviews.rationale: Institutional impartiality can be experienced as procedural fairness, but current sources are governance indicators and perception regressions rather than an independently identified institution-to-person effect.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Shared fairness wording, objective/perceived mismatch, and police-package scope prevent universal causal inference.
existingReviews.proposal: Specify observed/experienced impartial procedure, the procedural fairness facet, population and timing; retain all other facets unknown.

existingReviews.rationale: Differential enforcement can be noticed as unfair, but differential treatment may be judged justified under relevant standards; neither source isolates this objective source.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Legitimating beliefs, exposure visibility and group position can change interpretation; no invariant negative sign.
existingReviews.proposal: Require comparable cases, awareness, standards and precise fairness facet before a bounded directional proposal.

existingReviews.rationale: External oversight is a real institutional condition; its effect on institutional trust requires exposure/credibility and later trust measurement, absent from the cited perception-regression evidence.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Reverse causality and omitted variables explicit in OECD. Preserve governed PRC-048 segment, not a newly proved pathway.

existingReviews.rationale: Service capacity is not satisfaction with a service. OECD measures perceptions; WGI is a composite. Exact capacity→trust identification remains missing.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Common method, selection into services and political attitudes can explain association. Preserve PRC-049 segment unchanged.

existingReviews.rationale: Information about corruption can alter trust, but real corruption prevalence, trust and legitimacy are distinct; cited sources do not establish the exact negative legitimacy claim.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Petty versus grand informational treatments differ; no NGO-donation effect and no automatic rightfulness effect.
existingReviews.proposal: Require observed corruption in specified institution, independent legitimacy measure and time order; do not substitute trust or information for endpoints.

existingReviews.rationale: Specific norm perceptions can precede intentions, but assigned norm discrepancy and adolescent behavior syntheses do not establish isolated descriptive-norm→commitment effects.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Selection exceeded socialization in the adolescent synthesis; own behavior can shape perceived norms; reference group matters.
existingReviews.proposal: Restrict to specified behavior/reference group, independently measured prevalence/frequency appraisal and later intention; retain reverse/selection and non-universal conditions.

existingReviews.rationale: Perceived approval and intention are related, but broad subjective-norm manipulations can bundle descriptive/approval and personal attitudes.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Shared self-report/obligation wording and pressure/approval distinctions; not evidence of inevitable compliance.
existingReviews.proposal: Specify whose approval, which behavior, independent approval measure and later commitment; no approval→actual behavior shortcut.

existingReviews.rationale: Procedural-justice packages and organizational justice correlations support a research direction, not uniform causal effects of every fairness facet on rightfulness.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Specific policing legitimacy outcome not statistically conclusive; four of seven evaluations derive from RISE; trust/satisfaction gains are not legitimacy.
existingReviews.proposal: Limit proposed scope to named fairness facet and independently measured authority rightfulness; retain null legitimacy findings and package versus component uncertainty.

existingReviews.rationale: Rightfulness may support voluntary compliance intention but policing programs do not independently manipulate legitimacy and then identify its effect on intention.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Obligation-to-obey items can overlap intention; actual compliance is not intention; confounding and outcome mismatch remain.

existingReviews.rationale: Functional perceived support can buffer stress-related outcomes, while integration measures often show main effects; these are not identical causal routes into perceived stress appraisal.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Well-being/health outcomes differ from PSY-054 appraisal; support matching and same-method bias matter.
existingReviews.proposal: Require specified available-support facet and later demand-resource appraisal; distinguish main effect from exact stressor-edge moderation, with no inferred universal buffering.

existingReviews.rationale: Perceived rejection and low belonging share content; randomized ostracism changes both but does not independently randomize the perceived-exclusion mediator.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Simultaneous inverse scores and outsider items risk construct/measurement duplication; social exposure is a different source.
existingReviews.proposal: Retain noncausal/construct-overlap review with exact replacement unresolved; no retyping, inverse-equivalence or mediation implementation.

existingReviews.rationale: Perceived exclusion→HPA/sympathetic stress requires independent mediation and physiological measures. RDoC constructs/units supply no segment-specific causal estimate.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Neural activity, general need threat and subjective distress do not equal BIO-007; no new BIO-F02 audit or shortcut.

existingReviews.rationale: Individual willingness to accept vulnerability differs from group cooperation prevalence. Current sources concern collective action/diffusion rather than isolated exact trust.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Trust games overlap cooperation/risk measures; aggregation and selection unresolved; SRC509/SRC235 component duplication retained.

existingReviews.rationale: Norm-feedback experiments can influence individual behavior, but perceived norms are not independently randomized and group prevalence requires explicit aggregation.
existingReviews.nullContrary: 2016 study offers reverse behavioral-to-perceived-norm pathway analysis too; neither direction proven by mediation regression.
existingReviews.proposal: Retain time-indexed reciprocal process RP-NORM-PREVALENCE-001; require reference-group composition/window, causal mechanism and aggregation without double-counting individual contributions.

existingReviews.rationale: Trust in competence/integrity is distinct from rightful authority; OECD does not identify this mediator-to-legitimacy segment.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Common institutional object/items, reverse judgment and mixed legitimacy outcomes. Preserve shared PRC-048/049 lineage rather than duplicate segments.

existingReviews.rationale: Controlled ostracism exposure supports a bounded increase in perceived exclusion; exact game-aligned ratings converge in young-adult experiments.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Age-six non-detection, pseudo-random assignment in one study, short duration, demand/attribution and cultural transfer limits remain. Framework/source mismatches require later evidence completion, not new proposition.

existingReviews.rationale: Actual prevalence may inform perceived norm only when sampled/communicated; displayed survey statistics are not the actual group changing.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Selective observation, false consensus, delayed updating and denominator mismatch; COM-B/diffusion references do not isolate this edge.
existingReviews.proposal: Require perceived/observed exposure channel, matched behavior/group/window and later estimate; keep reciprocal process timing and no instantaneous equality.

existingReviews.rationale: Publicly expressed approval may inform perceived approval, but private beliefs and expression are not identical; audience and salience select whose views are seen.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Pluralistic ignorance, sanctions and reference-group choice; current framework/diffusion sources do not directly identify the perception effect.
existingReviews.proposal: Specify observed approval exposure and private perception measurement for matched group/behavior; no universal mapping or normative endorsement.

existingReviews.rationale: Contact quality could affect trust in a contact, but cited dehumanization/violence and topology-diffusion sources do not establish that exact person-target effect.
existingReviews.nullContrary: Cooperative/voluntary contact selection, baseline trust and trust-game proxy; quality may already contain favorable judgments.

existingReviews.rationale: SOC-096 is an external RDS: group-status difference within a common field. An independently perceived disparity could influence fairness, but cited RD/collective-action reviews do not identify that exact route.
existingReviews.nullContrary: HEIGHTENED_CAUSAL. Group A/B status inputs may themselves be self-report judgments; common method/shared evaluation, unknown temporal separation and aggregate/constituent double-counting require review.

hypotheses.question: Actual behavioral prevalence equals perceived descriptive norm.
hypotheses.reason: Reference group sampling, perception error and false consensus break identity.

hypotheses.question: Perceived exclusion independently causes lower belonging.
hypotheses.reason: Existing REL-PSY-018 review reused; randomized exposure is not randomized mediator, and outsider/excluded item overlap matters.

hypotheses.question: Withholding virtual ball passes changes perceived exclusion in the bounded task.
hypotheses.reason: Discovery links EA-CAND-PSY-LAYER-0005 and existing REL-SOC-062, not a new duplicate Relationship.

hypotheses.question: Comparative peer-drinking feedback changes perceived descriptive norms.
hypotheses.reason: EA-CAND-PSY-LAYER-0006 remains unknown pending exact frequency-versus-volume measure and contrast extraction.

hypotheses.question: Perceived approval of behavior is identical to anticipated approval of one's act.
hypotheses.reason: Current general approval and prospective personal contingent approval differ; no merger.

hypotheses.question: Corruption information changes institutional trust.
hypotheses.reason: Petty/grand effects differ; exact PSY-134 profile, sample and message specification insufficient for formal effect.

hypotheses.question: Randomizing corruption information proves actual corruption reduces legitimacy.
hypotheses.reason: Source and outcome substitutions: message != corruption prevalence; trust != rightfulness.

hypotheses.question: Subjective status associates with physical health.
hypotheses.reason: Mostly cross-sectional, stronger self-rated health association; exact Biological endpoint/SES-versus-relevant-group rank alignment unresolved.

hypotheses.question: Intranasal oxytocin increases trust in a specified person.
hypotheses.reason: Replication and proxy concerns; no universal effect or recommendation; no new biological target.

hypotheses.question: Interpersonal and institutional trust are the same Driver.
hypotheses.reason: Different objects, vulnerability and expectation profiles; source credibility/calibration likewise distinct.

hypotheses.question: Perceived support changes exclusion-to-physiological-stress effect.
hypotheses.reason: Buffering synthesis lacks the exact edge, moderator measure, aligned timing and independent segment evidence.

hypotheses.question: Adding contacts or arranging groups increases perceived available support.
hypotheses.reason: Network/received support and perceived availability differ; package evidence not isolated causal operation.

hypotheses.question: Sleep loss causes perceived exclusion.
hypotheses.reason: Sleep experiment primarily measured distancing/loneliness; exact exclusion/belonging targets not established.

hypotheses.question: Loneliness and low belonging are universal semantic inverses.
hypotheses.reason: Related but not matched definitions or reference groups; no missing entity created.

hypotheses.question: Group relative deprivation causes anger and collective action.
hypotheses.reason: RD instruments can include angry resentment; source is often association and mismatched group/person outcome level.

hypotheses.question: Status-gap RDS independently changes fairness appraisal.
hypotheses.reason: Reuse REL-SOC-067 review; formula does not entail appraisal, but shared judgment and temporal/selection risks unresolved.

hypotheses.question: Cultural orientation changes descriptive-norm effects on intention.
hypotheses.reason: Country/peer-type differences in associations do not identify exact cultural moderator or causal edge.

hypotheses.question: Ostracism → perceived exclusion → physiological stress pathway.
hypotheses.reason: Governed segments/reachability and RDoC categories do not identify transmitted causal mediation.

hypotheses.question: Physical warmth increases interpersonal trust.
hypotheses.reason: Screened thermal-cue work measures trust-game/prosocial choices; replication and exact-person vulnerability mismatch require follow-up.

hypotheses.question: Rank feedback changes perceived status.
hypotheses.reason: Distinguish comparative task rank from prestige/respect/influence in a relevant lasting group; no exact effect extraction.

hypotheses.question: Approval cues increase anticipated personal approval.
hypotheses.reason: Norm studies do not isolate prospective self-contingent approval; reference group and action remain unspecified.

hypotheses.question: Represent a procedural-fairness-facet effect as whole Perceived Fairness decrease/increase.
hypotheses.reason: Multidimensional target scope issue aligns with existing Layer feature-scope escalation; no production schema repair.

hypotheses.question: Trust ratings or logistic arrows prove trust causally produces legitimacy.
hypotheses.reason: OECD expressly cautions against causal interpretation; rightfulness remains distinct from trust.

hypotheses.question: A Cyberball occurrence proves later aggression or permanent exclusion.
hypotheses.reason: Occurrence/protocol, subjective response and downstream behavior are separate; no automatic trait change or network tie mutation.

hypotheses.question: Fear of missing out causally modifies the ostracism perception edge.
hypotheses.reason: Holte interaction terms were not detected, and trait FoMO not randomized; no formal moderator or new ontology entity.

canonicalSourceReviews.finding: 23-study self-other norm discrepancy synthesis; reference group, question specificity and norm type affect discrepancies.
Adolescent behavior associations, not intention manipulation; longitudinal selection stronger than socialization.
183-study organizational justice synthesis separates four facets; authority evaluation not necessarily legitimacy.

canonicalSourceReviews.access: Primary article abstract/introduction excerpt; PubMed has no abstract
canonicalSourceReviews.finding: Functional perceived support versus integration distinguishes buffering/main-effect interpretations; health/well-being not exact stress appraisal.
Need-to-belong review is conceptual background; no independent mediator manipulation assumed.
Trustworthiness dimensions and willingness-to-vulnerability distinct from actions or institutional trust.
Specific legitimacy result inconclusive; four of seven legitimacy evaluations share RISE experiment; package effects and indirect-outcome bias limits retained.

canonicalSourceReviews.access: Canonical DOI check and Crossref lookup unsuccessful
canonicalSourceReviews.finding: Named 2009 temporal need-threat work is not verified through stored Annual Review DOI. No replacement or source alteration.
31-study subjective-SES review mostly cross-sectional; stronger association with self-rated than biological health.
120 randomized Cyberball studies; pooled first/last outcomes exclude manipulation checks; broad effects do not supply exact exclusion-rating coefficient. Short-term moderation model challenged.
No experimental exclusion→HPA mediated segment established by construct vocabulary.
Units of analysis are not experimental causal evidence.
210-study RD synthesis; justice-affect content and level alignment influence associations; not objective status-gap causality.
Collective-action synthesis not independent person-trust or RDS-to-fairness identification.
WGI perception composites too coarse for specific reforms; no direct institution-to-person causal identification.

canonicalSourceReviews.access: Selected econometric-methods text and indexed PDF passage
canonicalSourceReviews.finding: Report expressly warns against causal regression interpretation: reverse causality, correlated perceptions and omitted variables.
Not used to support a retained candidate without checking exact work/claim alignment.
Named dehumanization/intergroup violence study is not direct contact-quality→person-trust evidence.
Bundled Centola/Jackson-Yariv reference not a generic source for trust, norm perception or ostracism; SRC235 component duplication unchanged.
Same COM-B work as SRC122; framework classification does not identify norm/prevalence reciprocal effects.
Use only prior verified extraction of experimental attitudes/norms/self-efficacy synthesis; no new extraction or isolated descriptive-norm guarantee.
Theory of planned behavior is not proof of every norm/intention causal direction.
Self-determination synthesis not direct availability-of-support intervention evidence.
TDF validation is not manipulation of perceived status or interpersonal trust.
